en: [318.4] (*194r4) Then all the Blessed Tathāgatas proclaimed this secret of the mystery of gnosis.
"Phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature, as stainless as space;
through the vajra of the knowledge of emptiness, there is the meditation on that which arises from emptiness.
They offered words of approval because of their yoga in accomplishing the tantra.
Excellent, excellent is the great knowledge, the most supreme of all expressions!
Excellent is the fierce Vajra-method that accomplishes the awakening of the Buddhas! Excellent is the non-dual yoga, the means for accomplishing the ever-higher stages!
Excellent is the yoga of certainty and the contemplation free from desire;
excellent, O Lord of the entire world, is the teacher of the Mahāyāna—
the supreme, most excellent tradition, the unsurpassed non-dual gnosis.
"Excellent is the Vajra-Guru, the teacher of the tantra of all yoginīs! Excellent is he who bestows supreme accomplishment upon the circles of the assembly! Thus they became silent.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Vajrasattva, and all those Tathāgatas; they rejoiced in what was spoken by the Blessed One regarding the *Ḍākaḍākinījālasamvara*, the supreme among the supreme [tantras] known as the *Krodharāja*.

Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter, the instruction on the reality of the single syllable and its meditative cultivation, from the *Abhidhānottara*, the Great King of Tantras, which is the most secret of secrets concerning the vows of names.
The Great King of Tantras named Abhidhānottarottara is completed.

[The Verse of Truth: "Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has declared their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa. In the year two hundred and fifty-seven, this King of Tantras was written by the virtuous Paramānanda. By this merit, may the world attain the state of the Vajradhātu! Thus ends the Mahātantra.
Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has declared their cause, as well as their cessation; thus speaks the Great Śramaṇa.

May there be prosperity! In the year 761, on the ninth day of the dark fortnight of Caitra, on a Tuesday, this was completed. It was written by Maṇideva, a resident of Śrī Cakrabāhāla—one with a broken back, a hunched neck, and burning eyes, looking downward; he has written this treatise so that it may be protected like a son. Just as it was seen by him, so has it been written by me. May it be auspicious for Jayamuni of the illustrious Śākya lineage at Xekājula.
